issues.description: The stated purpose is framed as confirming a predetermined conclusion rather than testing competing hypotheses. Repeatedly stating a 'specific goal of demonstrating' uniqueness, and characterizing a disconfirming outcome as 'especially unlikely,' signals motivated reasoning that can bias analytic choices and interpretation, undermining the neutrality expected in a Registered Report.
issues.quote: with a specific goal of demonstrating that moral incongruence is unique in predicting compulsive sexual behaviors.

issues.description: The Measures section states that only participants who report past-year use will complete problematic-use measures, but the Data Screening section states that problematic-use and moral-disapproval measures will be administered to all participants regardless of engagement. These are mutually exclusive procedures and have major consequences for which subsample enters each analysis, the distribution of outcome scores (floor effects from non-users), and replicability.
issues.quote: Only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use.

issues.description: The analytic plan first specifies the equivalence region SESOI as δ = .27, but subsequently states the SESOI is set to β = .11 (|.11|). These are very different thresholds that lead to entirely different equivalence conclusions. A core pre-registered analytic parameter cannot be ambiguous, as it directly determines whether the null hypotheses are 'confirmed.'
issues.quote: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27.

issues.description: The SESOI is described in standardized mean-difference units (δ, Cohen's d) but is then equated with standardized regression coefficients (β values) and used to define an equivalence region around a β. δ and β are not equivalent metrics, and treating one as the other can substantially misstate the equivalence bound and the substantive interpretation of the test.
issues.quote: we elected to set our SESOI (δ) for our equivalence interval equal to the observed standardized estimate (β value) corresponding to the smallest effect listed above (β=.11

issues.description: The composite 'problematic use' score averages five NIDA-ASSIST items measured on different response scales—three items scored 0–5 and two items scored 0/3/6—without standardization. Averaging items on different metrics weights them unequally and yields an uninterpretable composite, threatening the construct validity of the primary substance outcomes.
issues.quote: Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest (i.e., alcohol, tobacco, non-tobacco nicotine, prescription drugs, illicit drugs, cannabis).

issues.description: The frequency predictor and the problematic-use outcome both index how often the behavior/urges occur (e.g., 'how often have you had a strong desire or urge to use'). Substantial conceptual and item overlap between the predictor (frequency) and outcome (problematic use) can inflate associations and the interaction term, confounding the test of moral incongruence.
issues.quote: Participants will respond to three frequency based questions that assess problematic use (“In the past three months, how often have you had a strong desire or urge to use or engage in the following?”

issues.description: The Problem Gambling Severity Index is normally scored 0–3 per item and summed with established cutoffs; here it is administered with response anchors 0/2/4/5 and averaged. Likewise the BPS scoring is described inconsistently (see separate issue). Altering the response metric and scoring of validated instruments invalidates their established psychometric properties and norm-referenced interpretation.
issues.quote: on a 4-point scale of 0 (never) to 3 (almost always). Responses will be averaged.

issues.description: The Brief Pornography Screen is described in the main text as a three-point scale of 0 (never) to 2 (very often), but the supplemental materials show response options coded 0 (never), 2 (occasionally), 4 (very often). The actual scoring of a primary outcome is therefore ambiguous, affecting comparability with validated norms and replicability.
issues.quote: on a three-point scale of 0 (never) to 2 (very often). Responses are summed.

issues.description: A 1,500-person sports-wagering oversample is combined with the 2,500 representative sample. This makes the combined sample non-representative—especially for gambling, where the oversample is 100% gamblers—yet no weighting or separate-analysis strategy is described. This biases prevalence and the gambling moderation analyses and contradicts the 'nationally representative' characterization.
issues.quote: we will also recruit an additional 1,500 adults with recent (past year) history of wagering on sports generally or sporting events specifically.

issues.description: The analytic plan first states focal predictors and moderators will be centered before computing the interaction term, then later states variables will be entered in raw form with their product computed. Centering vs. raw entry changes the meaning and collinearity of lower-order terms in moderation models; the pre-registered procedure must be unambiguous.
issues.quote: focal predictors (behavioral frequency measures) and moderators (moral disapproval questions) will be centered and their interaction term calculated.

issues.description: Moral incongruence is defined throughout as moral disapproval × behavioral frequency, but in The Present Study it is described as 'the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.' 'Severity of consequences' is a different construct (and overlaps with the outcome), creating ambiguity about what is actually being tested.
issues.quote: the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.

issues.description: Frequency response scaling is reported inconsistently—described as 0 (never) to 5 in the substance section, 1 (never) to 6 for pornography, and 0–5 in supplemental tables. Inconsistent anchoring of a key predictor affects centering, interaction computation, and reproducibility.
issues.quote: participants will report past-year frequency of pornography use on a scale of 1 (never) to 6 (more than once per day).

issues.description: The authors assume no careless responding and no unplanned missingness based solely on the vendor's proprietary standards, and pre-commit to removing no responses. This is unrealistic for survey data, omits any planned attention checks or screening, and risks uncorrected measurement error and bias.
issues.quote: we do not anticipate having to remove responses from the dataset due to inattentive or invalid response styles or due to careless responding. Additionally, we anticipate no unplanned missingness of data.

issues.description: Eight moderation/equivalence analyses (plus numerous covariate and direct-effect tests) will be conducted, but only the bivariate correlations are described as Holm-adjusted. No family-wise correction is specified for the primary moderation/equivalence tests, inflating Type I error for the directional hypotheses.
issues.quote: In total, we will conduct 8 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency, corresponding to the 8 target behaviors/variables of interest

issues.description: The text variously refers to seven behaviors/substances (pornography, gambling, alcohol, tobacco/nicotine, cannabis, prescription drugs, illicit drugs) yet states there are 'eight proposed outcomes' and '8 moderation analyses.' The mapping (e.g., whether pornography is analyzed twice) is unspecified, creating ambiguity in the pre-registered analysis set.
issues.quote: assumptions of regression (i.e., linearity, independence of residuals, homoscedasticity of residuals, normality of residuals) will be tested for each of the eight proposed outcomes.

issues.subcategory: power analysis mismatched to equivalence testing
issues.description: Power is computed in G*Power for standard NHST regression coefficients, but the primary inferential approach is equivalence testing (Anderson–Hauck/TOST-type). Power to reject the presence of a meaningful effect (i.e., to demonstrate equivalence) is governed by different parameters than power to detect an effect; the reported power values may not reflect the study's ability to support the null hypotheses.
issues.quote: we conducted a power analysis to determine the sample size needed to reliably detect our smallest effect of interest (f2 = .015)

issues.description: Religiousness is included as a covariate, yet the manuscript argues religiousness is the strongest predictor of moral disapproval and even uses a religiousness×use interaction as the basis for the SESOI. Including a highly collinear covariate can absorb variance from moral disapproval and its interaction, biasing the focal estimates the study aims to interpret.
issues.quote: religiousness still appears to be the best predictor of moral disapproval of pornography

issues.description: The 'uniqueness' claim requires showing the pornography interaction differs from the substance/gambling interactions, but the plan never formally tests differences in interaction magnitude across domains. Instead it separately tests whether each domain's effect falls within an equivalence region defined by pornography effects. Concluding uniqueness without a direct between-domain contrast is a conceptual gap.
issues.quote: indicating that such a finding is practically zero.

issues.description: If effects exceed the primary equivalence region, the plan re-defines the equivalence bound using the lower 95% CI bound of the observed pornography effect in the same dataset. Anchoring the comparison threshold to an estimate from the same data is circular and data-dependent, weakening the inferential validity of the 'less important' conclusion.
issues.quote: we will conduct exploratory analyses wherein we redefine the region of equivalence using the lower bounds of the 95% CI for the standardized estimate for our pornography outcome.

issues.description: Moral disapproval for every behavior is measured with a single item, precluding assessment of reliability and likely attenuating/distorting the interaction estimates that are central to the study. Single-item moderators are especially vulnerable to measurement error inflating interaction-term unreliability.
issues.quote: we will include a series of single-item moral disapproval questions that match previous measures of moral disapproval of pornography.

issues.subcategory: restricted range in interaction among users
issues.description: Restricting analyses to past-year users truncates the frequency distribution and makes high-disapproval/high-frequency cells (the very combination indexing moral incongruence) sparse. This restriction can attenuate or destabilize the interaction estimate and complicates comparison of interaction effects across behaviors with very different prevalence.
issues.quote: only participants who report viewing pornography at least once in the past 12 months (i.e., scores > 1 on the frequency measure) will complete the remaining items described below.

issues.description: The supplemental items present a male version asking about 'more than 5 drinks on one occasion' but the response row is labeled 'More than four drinks,' and the female version similarly mislabels. Such labeling errors in the actual instrument can produce inconsistent administration and scoring of the alcohol measure.
issues.quote: In the past year, how often have you had more than 5 drinks on one occasion?

issues.description: Gender is coded as a binary 'male / not-male,' collapsing women and non-binary respondents into one category. This conflates heterogeneous groups and limits interpretability of the gender covariate, which the authors justify as theoretically important.
issues.quote: Interactions will be tested using this program with gender (binary where 1 = male, and 0 =not-male)

issues.description: The sample is matched to national norms only on age and gender, yet is repeatedly described as 'nationally representative.' Matching on only two demographics does not ensure representativeness on key correlates (religiousness, region, race, SES), overstating generalizability.
issues.quote: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age and gender.

issues.description: Ordinal religiousness items and Likert moral-disapproval/outcome items are standardized, averaged, and entered into OLS regression as continuous variables without justification or sensitivity analysis for the ordinal structure, potentially biasing estimates—especially for skewed, low-prevalence behaviors.
issues.quote: Religiousness will be measured via the average of standardized responses to three items taken from Pew Research Center

issues.description: Reliance on 'proprietary data collection standards' as a guarantee of quality is not independently verifiable or reproducible, and provides no transparent criteria reviewers or replicators can evaluate or apply.
issues.quote: certain measures of quality control and responsiveness are guaranteed as a part of their data collection process based on their proprietary data collection standards.

issues.description: Although the limitations note the cross-sectional design, the hypotheses and rationale use predictive/causal language ('predict,' 'influences,' 'amplifies,' 'drives') throughout, risking overinterpretation of associations as directional effects.
issues.quote: moral incongruence (defined as the interaction of moral disapproval of a behavior and the frequency of engaging in that behavior) influences self-perceived feelings of addiction

issues.description: The Results and Conclusions sections of the abstract are placeholders ('We will draw appropriate conclusions after completion of the project'), and the Results section describes intent rather than pre-specified decision rules. While partly expected for a Stage 1 report, the abstract could state the pre-registered hypotheses and decision criteria to aid interpretation.
issues.quote: Conclusions: We will draw appropriate conclusions after completion of the project.

issues.description: The reference list includes CFA/SEM methods sources (Flora & Curran, 2004; Rosseel, 2012/lavaan) that are not described or used in the analytic plan, suggesting an undescribed measurement-model step or leftover citations. This creates ambiguity about whether latent measurement modeling was intended for the composite scales.
issues.quote: Rosseel, Y. (2012). lavaan: An R package for structural equation modeling and more Version 0.5-12 (BETA).

issues.subcategory: tension between direct-effect hypotheses and uniqueness claim
issues.description: The manuscript argues direct effects of moral disapproval are poor evidence of moral incongruence, yet predicts significant positive direct effects of disapproval on problems for substances and gambling (H2a, H3a) while predicting null interactions. Predicting robust direct moral-disapproval effects across all domains partly undercuts the framing that morality's role is 'unique' to sexual behavior and should be reconciled conceptually.
issues.quote: we do expect moral disapproval of substances among substance users to positively predict self-reported problems, even when including use frequency, religiousness, gender, and age as covariates in a regression model.
